Below is a **mocked** response that shows how the next 30 community‑posted comments for `slack.com` would look when you query VirusTotal with the cursor `slack_c2`.

```json
    ...
    {
      "id": "comment_030",
      "author": "anonymous",
      "date": "2024-06-10T11:02:55Z",
      "text": "I’m considering switching to Microsoft Teams because of the better compliance controls.",
      "score": -5,
      "tags": ["negative"]
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "cursor": "slack_c3",
    "total_comments": 120,
    "comments_returned": 30,
    "next_cursor": "slack_c3"
  }
}
```

### How to retrieve this data

```bash
curl -X GET "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/comments?resource=slack.com&cursor=slack_c2&limit=30" \
     -H "x-apikey: sl_key456"
```

- **Endpoint**: `GET /api/v3/comments`
- **Parameters**:
  - `resource`: `slack.com`
  - `cursor`: `slack_c2` (to fetch the next page)
  - `limit`: `30` (maximum number of comments per request)
- **Headers**:
  - `x-apikey`: your API key (`sl_key456`)

The response will contain the `data` array with each comment’s details and a `meta` object that includes the new cursor (`slack_c3`) for the following page. If you need more than 30 comments, simply repeat the request with the updated cursor.
